relationships.evidence_quote: Importantly, these disruptions to lipid composition were largely prevented by treatment with carprofen (Supplementary Fig. 9a–j), specifically implicating MC38 tumor-driven inflammation in the disruption of circulating lipids.

relationships.subject: MC38 colorectal tumor
relationships.evidence_quote: Immunoreactivity for S100B—which is secreted by activated Schwann cells in neurodegenerative conditions32—was elevated in sciatic and intercostal nerves from MC38 mice and attenuated by carprofen

relationships.subject: MC38 colorectal tumor
relationships.evidence_quote: However, a significant increase in myelin decompaction (“onion bulb” formations) was seen in MC38 mouse nerves (Fig. 4g–i).

key_findings: MC38 colorectal tumor mice develop peripheral neuropathy with nerve fiber loss, myelin decompaction, plasma and nerve dyslipidemia and impaired motor coordination, without overt hypersensitivity.
Carprofen attenuated gait changes, S100B and lipid disruptions, implicating tumor-driven inflammation.
